Goals.Goal: **Recorded fact.** A permitting gate approve that records writes attribute baseCommit on that Decision, equal to git rev-parse HEAD at the first successful observation. evaluate stays git-free. The attribute is omitted when git cannot name HEAD and no prior value exists. Refuse, apply, and archive Decisions never carry it.

**Stable fact.** A later permitting approve does not write a different object name. It copies the first recorded value or omits the attribute if none exists yet. The Decision list only grows (RM-GOVERNED-PATH D9).

**Default universe.** review with argv token change and neither override, when a recorded baseCommit resolves, runs the scope audit over name-only paths that differ between that commit and the working tree, including untracked files, POSIX-normalized at the helper. inputSource is recorded-base, distinct from argv token base (still three-dot to HEAD).

**Honest weaker audit.** When argv token change is set, no override is set, and no recorded base exists, porcelain remains and both text and JSON carry the caveat sentence. An unresolvable recorded sha is unable-to-determine and does not fall back to porcelain.

**Decided here — attribute, not child, not sibling.** baseCommit is an attribute on the permitting approve Decision. A BaseCommit child is forbidden: both parseDecisionNode and validateLedgerDecisionsSection treat a non-Requirement child as ledger.invalid-decision, which would make the approve event unreadable and vacate the P3.7 trigger this record exists to create. A sibling section is the sidecar RM-GOVERNED-PATH D3 rejected. Historical Decisions without the attribute stay valid. parseDecisionNode copies a non-empty baseCommit attribute onto GateDecisionRecord and still returns invalid only for the children it already rejects.

**Decided here — who writes, when.** The observation runs in the record path (recordGateDecision / the approve command's record=true branch), never inside evaluateApproveGate. argv token record false writes no Decision and no baseCommit. First permitting approve with a resolvable HEAD writes that object name. A later permitting approve copies the first stored value when one exists; it never stores a different name. If the first permit had no git and a later permit can name HEAD, that later permit is the first observation and may write it. Newest-governs for permit lookup is unchanged and is not the reader for this fact. The reader is the first permitting approve Decision in document order whose baseCommit is non-empty (listGateDecisions).

**Decided here — universe and overrides.** Order: defined changedFiles (including empty) stays caller-owned; else non-empty argv token base stays three-dot name-only to HEAD via listFilesChangedAgainstBase (do not change that helper); else when argv token change is set and a recorded baseCommit resolves, use the new commit-versus-working-tree name-only set (diff-filter ACMR, plus untracked, same path normalize as the existing helpers); else porcelain. The two-dot phrase in the roadmap is the commit-versus-worktree set, not a change to argv token base. Do not reuse listFilesChangedAgainstBase for the recorded default: that helper stops at HEAD and would go blind on uncommitted work.

**Decided here — caveat and absence.** Exact caveat sentence, pinned (F44): no base commit — cannot attribute pre-existing changes. It appears in the Scope audit text line and in scopeAudit.reason when argv token change is set, no override is set, and no recorded base exists (porcelain ran, porcelain not-run, or git unavailable). It does not appear when the recorded universe ran, and it does not appear under an override. An unresolvable recorded sha is unable-to-determine naming that sha; it does not print this sentence (the fact exists; it does not resolve) and it does not fall back to porcelain (RM-AGENT-RELIABILITY D5; RM-GOVERNED-PATH D2.1 same posture). No new ReviewResult key.

**Decided here — what existing reports do.** Intentional: with a recorded resolvable base and no override, review.scope-outside-write-scope findings on paths that do not differ from that commit leave the report; undeclared paths that do differ still raise; after a clean commit of work since the base the scope audit runs instead of corr-169 not-run. Not changed: WriteEvidence scope audit, attempt-pair audit, unscoped review, argv token base, argv token changed-files, the any-C-* lifecycle exclusion, stay-audited durable trees. Historical bundles with an approve event and no baseCommit keep porcelain and gain only the caveat line.

**Decided here — F56 / F67 / F68 / F80.** signatureKey names the property: record-base, base-stable, review-universe, base-unresolved, caveat-text, caveat-json. Do not key on a test file stem. Two planned reds in one task must be able to fail alone. caveat-text and caveat-json are separate properties (F80): do not put both surfaces in one case that short-circuits. A task may plan at most three distinct kind-plus-key pairs. Do not state how many fail events a property implies except in AC-HEAD-RED (F75).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECORD-BASE: A permitting gate approve with recording on writes attribute baseCommit on that Decision equal to git rev-parse HEAD when that command succeeds. evaluateApproveGate still does not spawn git. Recording off writes no Decision and no attribute. A refuse approve, and every apply or archive Decision, omit the attribute. An unreadable HEAD at first observation omits the attribute (no empty value, no unknown token). parseDecisionNode returns a valid record when the attribute is present. listGateDecisions still treats the event as a permitting approve. **HEAD today:** Decision attributes are only gate and decision. **Failure conditions:** a child tag; writing the attribute from evaluate; writing it on refuse or apply; inventing a value when git fails; making parseDecisionNode invalid on the new attribute.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-BASE-STABLE: Given a permitting approve Decision that already carries baseCommit=A, a later permitting approve whose HEAD is B (B not equal A) writes either no baseCommit or baseCommit=A. It never writes B. The earlier Decision bytes are not rewritten. The reader (first permitting approve with a non-empty baseCommit) still returns A. **HEAD today:** a second approve appends another Decision with no baseCommit (live archive shape). **Failure conditions:** silently storing B; rewriting the first Decision in place; newest-governs becoming the reader for this fact.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REVIEW-UNIVERSE: review with argv token change, no overrides, and a resolvable recorded baseCommit runs the scope audit over the commit-versus-working-tree name-only set (inputSource recorded-base, baseRef equal to that sha). A path that differs from the commit and is outside ObservedWriteScope still raises review.scope-outside-write-scope. A path that does not differ and is not new untracked does not enter. Uncommitted new tracked and untracked paths since the commit do enter. After a clean commit of in-scope work since the base, the audit runs (not corr-169 not-run). Without a recorded baseCommit, corr 169 empty-porcelain not-run still holds. **HEAD today:** no recorded-base branch; clean tree is not-run. **Failure conditions:** calling listFilesChangedAgainstBase for this default; dropping untracked; leaving clean-tree committed work as not-run; changing unscoped review.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-UNRESOLVED: A recorded baseCommit that git cannot resolve makes the scope audit unable-to-determine. The reason names the sha. The audit does not run over porcelain. The caveat sentence from AC-CAVEAT-TEXT is absent. **HEAD today:** no reader, so a fixture attribute is ignored and porcelain runs. **Failure conditions:** silent porcelain fallback; using the no-base caveat sentence for a present-but-dead ref.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CAVEAT-TEXT: When argv token change is set, no override is set, and no recorded base exists, formatReviewResult prints the exact sentence no base commit — cannot attribute pre-existing changes on the Scope audit line (F44). The sentence is absent when recorded-base ran and absent under either override. **HEAD today:** the sentence is absent. **Failure conditions:** printing it only in a finding; swallowing it when findings is 0; printing it after a successful recorded-base run.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CAVEAT-JSON: Under the same conditions as AC-CAVEAT-TEXT, scopeAudit.reason contains that same sentence. No new ReviewResult top-level key appears. schemaVersion stays 1.0.0. **HEAD today:** scopeAudit.reason names porcelain absence or working-tree porcelain and does not contain that sentence. **Failure conditions:** text-only caveat; a new top-level JSON key; JSON silence while text speaks.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-OVERRIDES: Defined changedFiles (including empty) still wins and still names the empty set as caller-owned. Non-empty argv token base still uses listFilesChangedAgainstBase (three-dot to HEAD) and still ignores a recorded sha. Passing both override flags still refuses. WriteEvidence and attempt-pair audits still read the ledger, not this universe. **HEAD today:** already true (F45). **Failure conditions:** recorded-base overriding an explicit flag; changing the three-dot helper.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-HEAD-RED: Each of AC-RECORD-BASE, AC-BASE-STABLE, AC-REVIEW-UNIVERSE, AC-UNRESOLVED, AC-CAVEAT-TEXT, and AC-CAVEAT-JSON has a red recorded before its production edit, in its own tool round trip, with the failing test written first, under the signature keys named above. Never a red backed only by a grep, and never a retrospective red via stash. **Exempt (F45, named at authoring):** AC-OVERRIDES (already true at HEAD); AC-SUITE-AND-LINT (green at HEAD; close-time bar); allReviewCodes cardinality unmoved; localize excluded-review-code cardinality unmoved; README.md staying out; examples/ staying out; package.json version unchanged; token-accounting.ts unopened; listFilesChangedAgainstBase unmoved; evaluateApproveGate staying git-free; grammar Decision children staying Requirement-only. **HEAD today:** no baseCommit attribute is written; review has no recorded-base branch; the caveat sentence is absent. **Failure conditions:** a check that passes on pre-change HEAD sold as new behaviour; fail and pass in one tool call; AC-OVERRIDES or AC-SUITE-AND-LINT required to be red at HEAD; caveat-text and caveat-json reddened so the second fails naming the first (F68, F80).
